intent.tagline: The tracker takes the state. The documents keep the words.
intent.narration: CoBuilder knew what its slices meant and could not say what was next. The ladder lived in a markdown table that every session reread and any session could contradict. This design gives the state a store and leaves every document exactly where it was.

problem_solution.problem: Slice state, scores, and attempts lived in prose tables. Epic branches and pull-request numbers lived in hand-edited joins. Nothing answered what is next, what blocks what, or what changed while two sessions worked one ladder.
problem_solution.solution: One beads tracker per narrated repo. Programs, epics, and slices become issues with a namespaced metadata envelope. The ladder becomes blocked-by dependencies, readiness becomes bd ready, and the index rebuild gains one read.
problem_solution.narration: The mapping is deliberate about the line. Records with a stage, a score, or a position become issues. Records that are prose or external facts stay files and get pointers.

beats.text: Program, epic, slice, and decision become issues; pull requests, districts, and publications stay out with pointers.
Every issue carries metadata.cb with kind, version, and the consumer ids the viewer already uses.
Slice n blocks slice n+1, so bd ready names the next slice the table used to name by hand.

alternatives.option: Markdown tables as the only state
alternatives.rejected_because: State in prose races at whole-file grain and has no history.
Network-bound and wrong-grained; ADR-0029 already reads the pull request from GitHub.
It rebuilds readiness, gates, and sync that beads already ships.

architecture.narration: Beads sits under the index as the state layer. The scripts speak bd, the documents stay sources of record, and the viewer never learns the tracker exists.

beats.text: Sessions write state through bd commands with envelope files; bd is the only writer.
build_index.py reads bd list --json once, projects the same entities and joins, and writes the same index.
When bd is absent, scripts fall back to the file flow and the index projects from files alone.
